clue.text: Commotion as new edition of Chambers left 'hospital' out

indicators.note: a new edition reworks the text, so the letters of the dictionary's name are rearranged
the hospital letter is put out, taken away from the name

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A publisher's mix-up: the new Chambers dictionary has dropped the word 'hospital'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes H from CHAMBERS, leaving CAMBERS; L joins it and 'new edition of' rearranges the lot. Chambers is the British dictionary crossword setters favour.
explanation.definitionFit: A scramble is a disorderly rush or struggle, so it is a synonym of a commotion.

clue.text: Addicted and extremely skint, manage to get joints with difficulty

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
gout is a disease causing painful, swollen joints

explanation.surface: A broke drug user struggles to get hold of joints, as in cannabis cigarettes.
explanation.walkthrough: Skint is British slang for having no money. 'joints' looks like cannabis but is the body's joints.
explanation.definitionFit: Strung out is slang for being hooked on drugs, or in withdrawal, so it fits addicted.

clue.text: Pay for communist on ship

parts.note: red is the traditional label for a communist
re means on or concerning, as in letter headings
SS is steamship, a standard ship prefix

explanation.surface: A sailor asks for compensation for a communist on board.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a wrong is to make amends or compensate for it, as one pays for damage.

clue.text: Macho to eat head of insect? For the most part

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: macho means tough and masculine, that is manly

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A dare: is it macho to bite the head off a bug? Mostly, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Mainly means chiefly or largely, so it describes something true for the most part.

clue.text: Install new shed with external bolt for farm animals

indicators.note: the fastening sits on the outside, wrapping the other part

parts.note: a bolt is a fastening on a door, so a lock

indicators.note: to shed is to cast off, so the new letter is dropped

parts.note: to invest someone is to install them formally in office

explanation.surface: DIY instructions: put up a new garden shed with a bolt on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a garden building but it removes N; INVEST loses N to give IVEST, held in LOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Livestock are the domestic animals kept on a farm, such as cattle and sheep.

clue.text: Live on own, and conduct oneself properly

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: Advice to someone living alone: you can still keep up good manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling a child to behave means to act well and politely, the same sense as conducting oneself properly.

clue.text: Lay person mostly with bit of lust here

definitions.text: Lay person mostly with bit of lust here

indicators.note: most of the word is used, losing its last letter

parts.note: a lay brother is a member of a religious order who is not ordained

indicators.note: a bit of the word here is its first letter

explanation.surface: Where someone goes to be laid, with a dash of lust: a punning description.
explanation.walkthrough: As wordplay 'Lay person' is a lay brother, a monk not ordained; read whole, the clue describes a bawdy house.
explanation.definitionFit: A brothel is a house of prostitution, where people go to be laid with lust in mind.

clue.text: Part of stream from main server is initially lost

indicators.note: a lost letter is removed from the word

parts.note: the head waiter is the chief person serving in a restaurant

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tennis report: the top server's opening point is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main server' looks like tennis but is a restaurant's head waiter; 'initially' takes I from 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Headwaters are the source streams of a river, the uppermost part of its flow.

clue.text: Former soldier welcomes current soldier back in Socialist Republic

indicators.note: welcoming someone takes them inside, so one piece goes within

parts.note: vet is US slang for a veteran
I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: back means the soldier word is read in reverse

parts.note: a man is an ordinary soldier, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: An old soldier greets a serving one returning from a communist state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses MAN to NAM, also the slang name for this war.
explanation.definitionFit: Vietnam is officially the Socialist Republic of Vietnam, a one-party state in South East Asia.

clue.text: Staff cross when Oscar is dismissed

indicators.note: something dismissed is sent away, so the Oscar letter leaves the word for cross

parts.note: a rood is a crucifix or cross, especially one in a church
O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Employees are annoyed that their colleague Oscar has been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees and 'cross' like angry; the noun senses do the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff is a long stick or pole, and a rod is likewise a straight stick.

clue.text: I ignore VAT being fiddled in rally

indicators.note: accounts that are fiddled are tampered with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trader admits dodging value added tax by cooking the books.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is Britain's value added tax, a sales tax; 'fiddled' (falsified) suits tax evasion.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally someone is to revive their spirits or strength, which is what invigorating them does.

clue.text: Provokes son, which is unnecessary

parts.note: to needle someone is to goad or provoke them
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent is told that winding up their boy serves no purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Something needless is not required, a direct synonym for being unnecessary.

clue.text: Cutting heroin with family from Dallas

parts.note: H is slang for heroin
the Ewings are the oil family in the US soap opera Dallas

explanation.surface: A drug dealer cuts heroin alongside a Texan family's operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' heroin suggests diluting a drug, but here it means chopping.
explanation.definitionFit: To hew is to chop with an axe or blade, so hewing is cutting wood or stone.

clue.text: Exclude acoustic covers

indicators.note: the outer word acoustic covers, that is contains, the letters wanted

explanation.surface: A music review: acoustic cover versions are left off the album.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' looks like cover versions of songs; it signals the letters inside 'acoustic'.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to drive them out, so excluding them from a place or post.

clue.text: Essentially, stop and rate the French hierarchical system

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its middle letters

parts.note: tempo is the rate or speed of a piece of music
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French pecking order is briefly summed up, with a halt and a grading.
explanation.definitionFit: Low on the totem pole is an idiom for low rank, so the figure stands for a hierarchy.

clue.text: Jacket I am beginning to embellish to get better rate of pay

parts.note: a doublet is a close-fitting jacket worn by men in Tudor times
I'm is the contraction of I am

indicators.note: the beginning of the next word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tailor plans to add embroidery to a jacket and hopes to earn more.
explanation.definitionFit: Double time is overtime paid at twice the usual hourly wage, an improved rate for extra hours.

clue.text: Desire for Gore statue to be placed outside toilet by Democrat leader in Louisiana

indicators.note: the statue word goes outside, enclosing the others

parts.note: a bust is a sculpture of head and shoulders
loo is British slang for toilet
D is the abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A statue of Al Gore, the US Democrat, is planned near a Louisiana toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: Gore is capitalised to suggest Al Gore, the Democratic US vice-president, but means spilt blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodlust is a craving for violence and killing, a hunger for blood and slaughter.

clue.text: Perhaps post-Brexit tariffs restricting pub, of course, in Western Asia

definitions.note: a watercourse in the Middle East

indicators.note: restricting confines, so the outer piece holds the pub

parts.note: EU rates suggests the duties Britain charges on goods from the European Union since leaving it, hence perhaps
PH is public house on British maps

explanation.surface: After Brexit, tariffs squeeze pub trade, and of course the Middle East too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally'; 'course' is the definition, a river's course, with 'of' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Euphrates is a great river flowing through Turkey, Syria and Iraq, a watercourse of the region.

clue.text: Make Union pay church to accept introduction of economic strike in recession

indicators.note: the church payment takes in, or accepts, a letter inside it

parts.note: to tithe is to pay a tenth of one's income to the church

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter
receding means going backwards, so the word for strike is read in reverse

parts.note: to tonk is British slang for hitting hard, especially a ball

explanation.surface: A trade union story: pay, a church, an economic downturn and a strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make Union' is a capitalised trade union disguise for marriage; 'in recession' turns TONK into KNOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting married is the joining of two people in wedlock, a union made in a ceremony.

clue.text: The majority of stupid guards make droning sound, being cruel

indicators.note: guarding something surrounds it, so the outer piece holds the other
most of the word is used, its last letter going

parts.note: inane means silly or stupid
to hum is to make a low continuous drone

explanation.surface: Most guards are dim and hum tunelessly while treating prisoners badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link word joining the wordplay to the definition 'cruel'.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhuman means lacking human pity or kindness, hence brutal and cruel.

clue.text: Customer ordered nudes with expression of hesitation

indicators.note: putting things in order rearranges them, so these letters are shuffled

parts.note: er is the sound people make when they hesitate

explanation.surface: A buyer hesitantly admits having ordered nude pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like 'bought' but it rearranges NUDES to ENDUS.
explanation.definitionFit: An end user is the person or company who finally uses a product, so a customer.

clue.text: Tuppence divided up in bank

parts.note: split the word as tup and pence: a tup is a ram, and pence abbreviates to P

explanation.surface: A child's two pennies are shared out after being saved in a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divided up' tells you to cut Tuppence into TUP (a ram, or male sheep) and PENCE (P), giving RAM + P.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank can be a slope or incline, and a ramp is a sloping surface joining levels.

clue.text: Neat gin? Surprisingly, it can stimulate an immune response

definitions.text: it can stimulate an immune response

indicators.note: a surprising result is unexpected, so these letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Undiluted gin, surprisingly, sets off the body's defences.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigens are foreign substances that the immune system recognises and makes antibodies against.

clue.text: Got lucky with female Evangelist on date

parts.note: Luke is one of the four Gospel writers

explanation.surface: A woman and a gospel writer get lucky on a date.
explanation.definitionFit: A fluke is a lucky chance, so to fluke something is to succeed by good fortune.

clue.text: Discredited Welsh politician hides in outhouse

indicators.note: the politician hiding in the outbuilding sits inside its letters

parts.note: a shed is a small outbuilding
AM was Assembly Member, a member of the Welsh Assembly

explanation.surface: A disgraced politician from Wales lies low in a garden outbuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: Being shamed means being publicly disgraced, so one's reputation is discredited.

clue.text: Admirer of procrastinator's mantra?

definitions.meaning: a worshipper of images, or loosely a devoted fan
someone who puts things off keeps saying they will get it done later

explanation.surface: Someone is a fan of the motto of those who always delay.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater worships an idol, and by extension is an excessive admirer of anyone.

clue.text: Crazed idiot's run out in front of lorry

indicators.note: the first part is placed in front of the vehicle word
the run letter is out, removed from the word

parts.note: a moron is an idiot, with the possessive giving the S
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
a truck is the US word for a British lorry

explanation.surface: A fool is run over after stepping out in front of a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run out' looks like a cricket dismissal, but it removes R from MORONS, leaving MOONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonstruck once meant driven mad by the moon, so it is a synonym of being crazed.

clue.text: Devastate German for good

definitions.meaning: to ... a building is to destroy its insides, or to upset someone badly

explanation.surface: A German says something is devastating for good, that is, permanently.
explanation.definitionFit: Gutted in British slang means devastated, and fire can gut a house, wrecking it.

clue.text: Working, stopping 11 earning

indicators.note: refers to 11 across, whose definition is cutting: the letters wanted are cut out of the words either side

parts.note: no coincidence: this word gives the first half of the letters hidden across it and the next word
gives the second half of the hidden run, its last four letters cut away

explanation.surface: Someone at work has stopped earning money.
explanation.walkthrough: A hidden word: '11' stands for 11-across's definition, 'Cutting', the signal to cut the answer from 'stopping' and 'earning' either side of it; it is shown as a deletion because the indicator sits inside the run.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine in gear is engaged and running, so it is working rather than idle.

clue.text: Maybe undergraduates' exploits overwhelming disheartened debutante

definitions.note: undergraduates are an example of people in higher education, hence maybe; the possessive is surface only

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so the first word surrounds the second

parts.note: stunts are daring feats or exploits

indicators.note: a word losing its heart keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: University pranks overwhelm a demoralised young society woman at her coming-out.
explanation.walkthrough: A debutante is a young upper-class woman entering society.
explanation.definitionFit: Undergraduates are one kind of people studying at university, so they exemplify the wider class.
